D001_l001.question:
A 39-year-old single female, employed as a pharmacist, presents with a 1-year and 5-month history of persistent difficulties with attention, task completion, and regulation of activity and impulse control. She reports a long-standing pattern of symptoms beginning in childhood, with notable challenges in academic settings involving failure to attend to detail, frequent careless errors in work, and difficulty maintaining focus during tasks requiring sustained mental effort. She often fails to follow through on work responsibilities and household duties, becoming sidetracked before completion. Daily forgetfulness is evident, including missed appointments, unpaid bills, and neglected errands. Distractibility by external stimuli and internal thought processes further interferes with concentration.

Clinically significant hyperactivity and impulsivity are also present. She describes a chronic sense of inner restlessness, despite minimal overt motor activity, and an inability to relax during leisure time. Others have observed her as “always on the go,” as if driven by internal propulsion. She frequently interrupts conversations and has trouble waiting for her turn in social or professional settings. These symptoms occur across multiple settings, cause marked impairment in occupational and social functioning, and were present before age 12, with retrospective confirmation of childhood onset.
